title: Mediating gates between polar molecules using microwave-dressed Rydberg atoms
authors: Bas Gerritsen, Sean R. Muleady, Arghavan Safavi-Naini, Alexey V. Gorshkov, Jeremy T. Young
abstract: We propose a scheme for mediating many simultaneous, fast entangling gates between pairs of polar molecules using Rydberg atoms. By using microwave drives, the dipolar interactions between Rydberg atoms are nullified. Using the freedom left in the microwave dressing parameters, the Rydberg van der Waals interactions are minimized and the Rydberg-molecule interaction is tuned into resonance, allowing for the mediation of a modified iSWAP gate between molecules. In the example of mediating gates between $\rm{{}^{23}Na {}^{133}Cs}$ molecules with $\rm {}^{133}Cs$ atoms, the gate is more than two orders of magnitude faster than an equivalent direct molecule-molecule gate. We model the decay of the dressed Rydberg states and the motion of the atom and molecules and obtain a leading-order estimate of the resulting gate infidelities. Finally, we show that by detecting the state of the Rydberg atom after a gate, a subset of gate errors can be converted into erasure errors and mitigated by post-selection or quantum error-correction.
summary: This paper details a theoretical scheme to achieve fast, simultaneous entangling gates between polar molecules by mediating the interaction through microwave-dressed Rydberg atoms. By carefully tuning the microwave dressing parameters, the detrimental dipolar interactions are suppressed, allowing a resonant iSWAP gate to be implemented. The results show significant speedups over direct coupling and propose error mitigation strategies using state detection.
main_problem: The paper proposes a method to mediate fast, simultaneous entangling gates between pairs of polar molecules using Rydberg atoms.
main_result: The mediated gate is predicted to be significantly faster (by $>10^2$) than direct molecule-molecule gates, and gate errors can be partially mitigated using post-selection based on Rydberg atom state detection.
method: The scheme utilizes microwave dressing to nullify detrimental dipolar interactions between Rydberg atoms and tune the Rydberg-molecule interaction into resonance to mediate a modified iSWAP gate.
model_or_system: The system involves polar molecules and Rydberg atoms, modeled using Hamiltonians describing dipolar, van der Waals, and resonant molecule-Rydberg interactions. The dynamics are analyzed using master equations to account for decay and motion.
key_observables: Gate speed ($t_G$), gate infidelity ($1-F$), and post-selection success-weighted fidelity ($ ar{F}_{ps}$).
important_parameters: Microwave dressing parameters ($\alpha, \Omega_\pi$), molecular and atomic separation distances ($r_{Rm}$), and interaction strengths ($J$).
main_assumptions: The method relies on engineering dressed states to achieve destructive interference of dipolar interactions, and assumes the ability to model motion and decay using master equations.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the energy level diagrams for molecular and Rydberg atoms, showing the resonant excitation exchange mechanism and the microwave dressing scheme used to nullify dipole-dipole interactions.
paper_structure: The paper develops the theoretical framework by first introducing the dressing scheme to nullify Rydberg-Rydberg interactions, then deriving the resonant interaction Hamiltonian for the iSWAP gate, and finally analyzing gate performance by modeling decay and motion.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses the engineering of quantum gates in complex molecular systems using highly controllable Rydberg platforms, which is a major frontier in quantum simulation and quantum computing.
